label: Q01
question: Thirteen TOC values lie between 2,077 and 2,208 umol/L, 20 to 60 times the median (61.5 umol/L) and in the range of seawater dissolved inorganic carbon. Are they valid, or did inorganic carbon survive the acidification/sparging step? We propose an upper bound of toc valid_max = 1000 umol/L, which would drop them.
context: Observed in table_253.csv (EDI rev 3, 2026-10-06): 99th percentile 111 umol/L; 20 further values lie between 300 and 800 umol/L. The 13 values come from 5 cruises 2015-07 to 2017-08, at both inshore (e.g. 2015-10-29-C-32OC cast 28, line 86.7 station 33, four depths 2-51 m, 2,077-2,103 umol/L) and offshore stations (2017-08-01-C-33SR cast 42, line 86.7 station 100, 85 m, 2,089 umol/L). The ingest publishes them until this is answered; valid_min = 0 is registered, valid_max is not.
proposed_answer: Declare toc valid_max = 1000 umol/L, so the 13 values near 2,100 umol/L are dropped as analytical failures; values below 1,000 are kept.

label: Q02
question: 50 bottles carry more than one TOC row (46 with 2, 4 with 4). Are these replicate analyses of one water sample? In 2014-07-06-C-32NM cast 21, bottles 3 and 4 (both 3,498 m) list the same four values (40.4, 45.7, 46.3, 50.6 umol/L): are those four analyses split across the two bottles?
context: The ingest keeps one sample per bottle and publishes every row as its own obs (not averaged), so a bottle with replicates has 2 or 4 toc values. Some replicate pairs differ a lot, e.g. 2008-08-14-C-32NM cast 9 bottle 20 at 10 m: 60.0 and 81.1 umol/L.

question: What does 'TOC CV (%)' measure: the coefficient of variation of replicate injections of one sample? Should values with a high CV be flagged? (59 rows have none; 6 exceed 10%, up to 43.8%.)
context: Not published until answered. If it is the CV of the injections behind each reported value, it could be published as the value's precision (measurement_prec = TOC x CV / 100).
